thread:
Alice Ng: Quick sync — I pulled together customer asks on geo routing + tenant isolation and sketched launch hypotheses. Need prioritization + gating by EOD Friday.

Omar Patel: Nice, can you drop the hypotheses here so we can react? :eyes:

Alice Ng: Sure — copying the short list and proposed acceptance criteria. High level: three contract levels we heard from customers: 1) best-effort (hosted routing, shared capacity), 2) committed (reserved capacity + region affinity), 3) isolated (tenant-dedicated cells, data residency). Hypotheses: 
```
- H1: Most mid-market customers will accept committed if latency within 20% of hosted and cost delta < 2x. Acceptance: pilot with 3 customers, <20% latency increase vs hosted.
- H2: Enterprise regulated customers require isolated cells + KMS + audit logs; will pay 3-5x for isolation if SLA and compliance certs present. Acceptance: legal/security checklist + 2 PO commitments.
- H3: Multi-region failover w/ sticky affinity will reduce cross-region egress by >60% for geo-heavy customers. Acceptance: simulation with representative traffic reduces egress metric.
```

Casey L: I like those. For H1 we need to define what "latency within 20%" means (p95 token or end-to-end?). Suggest p95 generation latency for 512-token median workload.

Alice Ng: Good call. Update: p95 generation latency for 512 tokens.

Priya Singh: Ops note: committed capacity implies reservation + autoscale policy. We'll need clear rollout plan so we don't overcommit GPUs. Can we add acceptance of autoscale SLOs? e.g., 99.5% of bursts handled within 30s of demand spike.

Alice Ng: Added autoscale SLO for committed.

Omar Patel: On the isolated cells ask — we should enumerate non-functional requirements (NFRs) customers will expect: KMS integration, audit logs, network MRI (VPC peering), compliance report. Also migration path from committed -> isolated.

Alice Ng: Agreed. Proposed gating checklist for isolated: 
```
- KMS integration verified in staging (customer key wrap test)
- Audit log retention >= 1 year configurable
- Network isolation tests (egress block, dedicated subnet)
- Operational runbook + DR test passed (tenant failover < 10m)
- Pricing + contract template approved by legal
```

Casey L: DR test < 10m seems ambitious for initial launch. Maybe set target < 30m for GA and < 10m as stretch goal. Many infra changes needed.

Priya Singh: +1 to Casey. Also need capacity accounting for isolation — how do we transition customers off shared pools? That affects launch sequencing.

Alice Ng: Good points. Update gating: GA DR target <30m, stretch <10m. I'll flag capacity migration as dependency.

sre-bot: incident:autoresponder — FYI, cross-region traffic surge test scheduled for 1765000100; this will exercise routing fallback.

Omar Patel: Perfect timing — we can capture telemetry for H3. Who owns the simulation? @Priya Singh?

Priya Singh: I can own the sim, will coordinate with Ops to generate region-skewed load and collect egress metrics.

Casey L: Prioritization ask: do we push committed before isolated? My recommendation: committed -> routing/control-plane improvements -> isolated. Committed buys us revenue and reduces churn; isolated has bigger infra cost.

Alice Ng: My tentative priority aligns with Casey. We should validate with 2 sales leads (ask them to confirm willingness to sign committed contracts). Omar, can you run short customer check-in?

Omar Patel: Yep — will ping three existing mid-market accounts this week and report back by Thu.

Alice Ng: Thanks. Final ask for this thread: reactions on prioritization and gating by EOD Friday. If no objections we'll lock roadmap ticket and start scoping spikes for autoscale + KMS integration. :white_check_mark:

Casey L: +1

Priya Singh: +1

Omar Patel: +1

Alice Ng: Great — I'll create the roadmap issue and link the gating checklist.
